method: Viewed actual public ICRSP article Commentaires section, specifically the named passage or opening paragraph, for 25 distinct source URLs. This is human-directed topic extraction from source prose, not an automated category match; not all author panels were read. No text reproduction.

records.observedEditorialSubject: The introduction joins John 10's Good Shepherd, Petrine pastoral care, and a Eucharistic application.
records.publicationGate: Do not present an Office homily as an independently verified patristic original; compare the existing Sunday Mass explanation.

records.observedEditorialSubject: The site juxtaposes the Sunday wedding-banquet Gospel with Corpus Christi and a Samuel narrative taken from the Office.
records.publicationGate: The text explicitly calls the Corpus Christi octave association pre-1955; separate Mass readings from Office analogy.

records.observedEditorialSubject: The introduction explains priestly ordination, the St Peter station, Joel, the three youths in the furnace, and Ember Saturday's extended lessons.
records.publicationGate: Keep each lesson and its order attached to the exact approved Mass form; source's general statement is not a 1962 lectionary certification.

records.observedEditorialSubject: The website associates September Ember fasting with seasonal thanksgiving and Zechariah's fourth, fifth, seventh, and tenth-month fasts.
records.publicationGate: Historical claims of apostolic origins and precise modern Ember calculations require separate evidence.

records.sourceTitle: St Jean Damascène, Confesseur et Docteur
records.observedEditorialSubject: The page dates the Latin calendar observance and connects John Damascene with iconoclasm and the defence of holy images.
records.publicationGate: Guéranger's period polemic about Byzantium is not neutral saint biography; separate it from sourced doctrine and modern factual dates.

records.sourceTitle: St Léon I, Pape, Confesseur et Docteur
records.observedEditorialSubject: The introduction distinguishes Leo's death date, historical liturgical feast dates, and his Doctor title; Guéranger links him to the Christological controversies.
records.publicationGate: Check the 1962 feast and historical date claims separately; do not import first-nocturn Office material as a Mass reading.

records.sourceTitle: St Paulin de Nole, Evêque et Confesseur
records.observedEditorialSubject: The page relates Paulinus' Bordeaux origin, Nola connection, and conversion through devotion to St Felix, with an account of old feast ranks.
records.publicationGate: Biographical offices and dates as reported by Guéranger require independent historical corroboration; pre-John XXIII Office readings are not 1962 readings.

records.sourceTitle: St Cyrille d’Alexandrie, évêque, confesseur et docteur
records.observedEditorialSubject: The commentary associates Cyril's defence of the divine maternity with Christ's personhood and a New Eve typological reading.
records.publicationGate: Separate Cyril's attested teaching from Guéranger's rhetoric and Marian application; do not attribute the commentary wording directly to Cyril.

records.observedEditorialSubject: The hosted article defines the title Doctor of the Church and includes a list numbering 38 Doctors.
records.publicationGate: The present-day tally and female Doctors include later proclamations; do not use the list to define 1962 Mass formularies or feast ranks.

records.sourceSectionLocator: Présentation / In Diœcesi Nanceiensi et Tullensi
records.observedEditorialSubject: The page specifies dioceses of Nancy-Toul, Saint-Dié, Verdun and Strasbourg and provides a locally scoped April 19 Mass formulary.
records.publicationGate: Do not create a universal 1962 observance, canonical Mass or new place record from a regional text; verify jurisdiction and rank.

records.sourceTitle: St Jean (27 décembre, 3ᵉ jour dans l’Octave de la Nativité)
records.observedEditorialSubject: The introduction discusses early regional differentiation of St John's December 27 feast and traditions about James and the Armenian calendar.
records.publicationGate: Historical martyrology reception is not evidence of current universal Roman rank; distinguish historical references.

records.sourceTitle: 29 décembre (5ᵉ jour dans l’Octave de la Nativité, St Thomas Becket)
records.observedEditorialSubject: The introductory note explicitly contrasts pre-John XXIII St Thomas Becket celebration with the post-1960 Nativity-octave weekday and commemorations.
records.publicationGate: Confirm the cited rubric §68 and exact 1962 collision handling before changing Calendar rules or Mass Propers.

records.observedEditorialSubject: The page associates Fourth Sunday after Easter with Christ's Ascension, the Spirit of truth, and the Mass Epistle and Gospel.
records.publicationGate: Keep Holy Spirit devotional explanation distinct from the proper readings of the Sunday; check owner for existing text.

records.observedEditorialSubject: The source explicitly identifies the earlier name Sunday within the Ascension octave, with an Augustinian spiritual ascent meditation.
records.publicationGate: Do not recreate a suppressed octave or assert original Augustinian locus without independent collation.

records.sourceSectionLocator: Introduction – Le Mystère de la Rédemption opening
records.observedEditorialSubject: The long season introduction relates Septuagesima to the paschal redemption cycle and distinguishes Incarnation and Redemption emphases.
records.publicationGate: This is a thematic introduction, not a distinct Mass day or an instruction to change seasonal computation.

records.observedEditorialSubject: The page describes Pentecost as the Spirit's manifestation in the formation of the Church and introduces a Roman station context.
records.publicationGate: Verify the station, proper and any historical vigil distinctions against the 1962 sources; do not conflate day, vigil and octave.

records.observedEditorialSubject: The page explicitly describes the abolition in 1955 of the historically rich Epiphany octave and its Office readings.
records.publicationGate: Former octave days and pre-1955 Office materials are historical only, not current 1962 calendar entries.

records.observedEditorialSubject: The introduction traces the apostles' joint observance to the dedication of the Roman Basilica of the Holy Apostles and translations of relics.
records.publicationGate: Confirm the feast date for the 1962 calendar and independently verify historical dedication and relic claims.

records.sourceTitle: Ss. Cyrille et Méthode, évêques et confesseurs
records.observedEditorialSubject: The page connects Cyril and Methodius with evangelisation of the Slavs and describes feast placement changes from July 5 to July 7, plus a modern co-patronage reference.
records.publicationGate: Do not treat a 1980 co-patronage proclamation as the authority for 1962 date/rank; source the hagiographic details separately.

records.observedEditorialSubject: The introduction contrasts two older Roman stations with the eventual July 29 feast of Martha and the Magdalene octave association.
records.publicationGate: Historical station associations are not proof of modern sacred-place records or 1962 feast collision rules.

records.sourceTitle: Dédicace de l’Archibasilique du Très Saint Sauveur
records.observedEditorialSubject: The website traces the Nov 9 Lateran dedication feast's later liturgical rank and explicitly discusses separate basilica dedication Office readings.
records.publicationGate: Keep Lateran and the November 18 basilicas distinct; Office homily comparisons do not equate to current Mass formularies.

records.sourceTitle: St Joseph, époux de la bienheureuse Vierge Marie, confesseur
records.observedEditorialSubject: The introduction surveys distinct ancient and Eastern feast patterns and the Western March 19 reception of St Joseph.
records.publicationGate: Historical assertions and Eastern rite dates are context only; do not overwrite 1962 Roman feast with other calendars.

records.sourceSectionLocator: Commentaire (Dom Pius Parsch, Le guide dans l’année liturgique) opening
records.observedEditorialSubject: The named Parsch panel explains the 1942 papal Common instituted under Pius XII and the Si diligis me Mass theme with Petrine shepherd imagery.
records.publicationGate: Verify the 1962 Common form and exact quotation provenance; Parsch's French text and papal excerpts lack reproduction/edition clearance.

records.observedEditorialSubject: The page recounts Lorraine-born Augustin Schoeffler's missionary formation and 1851 martyrdom in Tonkin, under a May 6 source heading.
records.publicationGate: Separate contemporary canonization and diocesan observance from the 1962 universal Sanctoral; source detailed biography independently.

records.observedEditorialSubject: The page treats St Don/Donat as a Lorraine martyr with lost Acts, later local traditions, and a local commemorative Mass with seasonal alternatives.
records.publicationGate: Traditions and reported miracles are not independent historic fact; do not promote local commemoration or Mass to universal 1962 use.
